headline: Learned models predict P450 metabolism sites, MS2 identifiability, and peak-node alignment
label: Learned Predictors For Metabolite Analysis
summary: Upstream decisions and local substructure correspondences are now predicted from partial data, not only from final identifications.
synthesis: The three preprints share a common thread: learned models infer molecular or acquisition-level quantities from indirect or partial inputs rather than direct readouts. ATTNSOM predicts atom-level sites of metabolism for cytochrome P450 isoforms using a shared graph encoder with cross-isoform attention, sharing information across isoforms rather than modeling each separately. The PU-learning framework predicts whether an MS2 scan will be identifiable from preceding MS1 spectra and acquisition parameters alone, trained on more than 8M Orbitrap metabolomics records. FLARE contrastively aligns spectral peaks with molecular graph nodes for MS/MS annotation, reporting 43.15% rank@1 on MassSpecGym with interpretable local spectra-molecule correspondences. What is new is the shift toward predicting upstream decisions and local substructure correspondences from partial data, rather than only final identifications.
